steps: Metals contain free electrons that can move throughout the metal.
When heated, these electrons gain energy and transfer it rapidly to other electrons and metal particles.
In this way, heat travels through the metal.
items.finalAnswer: Metals conduct heat through the movement of free electrons.

steps: Nitrogen forms five oxides.
Their formulae are N₂O, NO, N₂O₃, NO₂ and N₂O₅.
items.finalAnswer: Nitrogen forms five oxides: N₂O, NO, N₂O₃, NO₂ and N₂O₅.

steps: A double displacement reaction takes place when aqueous sodium bromide is treated with aqueous silver nitrate.
Silver bromide is formed as a pale yellow precipitate, while sodium nitrate remains in solution.
NaBr(aq) + AgNO₃(aq) → AgBr(s) ↓ + NaNO₃(aq)
items.finalAnswer: A pale yellow precipitate of AgBr forms.

steps: Iodine molecules (I₂) are larger and have more electrons than chlorine molecules (Cl₂).
The forces of attraction between iodine molecules are stronger than those between chlorine molecules.
More energy is needed to overcome these forces in iodine, so iodine is a solid at room temperature, whereas chlorine is a gas.
items.finalAnswer: Iodine is solid because its larger molecules have stronger intermolecular forces than Cl₂ molecules.

steps: An ionic bond is formed by the complete transfer of one or more electrons from one atom to another.
The atom that loses electrons forms a positive ion, while the atom that gains electrons forms a negative ion.
The electrostatic force of attraction between these oppositely charged ions is called an ionic bond. For example, sodium transfers an electron to chlorine to form Na⁺ and Cl⁻ in NaCl.
A covalent bond is formed when two atoms share one or more pairs of electrons.
For example, two chlorine atoms share a pair of electrons to form a Cl₂ molecule.
items.finalAnswer: An ionic bond forms by electron transfer and attraction between oppositely charged ions; a covalent bond forms by sharing electron pairs.

items.figure: Draw a regular arrangement of alternating Na⁺ and Cl⁻ ions in a three-dimensional cubic lattice. Show each Na⁺ ion surrounded by six Cl⁻ ions and each Cl⁻ ion surrounded by six Na⁺ ions. Label the ions and indicate that the oppositely charged ions are held together by electrostatic attraction.
steps: NaCl crystal consists of a regular, three-dimensional arrangement of Na⁺ and Cl⁻ ions.
The ions alternate so that each Na⁺ ion is surrounded by six Cl⁻ ions and each Cl⁻ ion is surrounded by six Na⁺ ions.
The oppositely charged ions are held together by strong electrostatic forces of attraction.
items.finalAnswer: In a NaCl crystal, Na⁺ and Cl⁻ ions are arranged alternately in a three-dimensional lattice, with each ion surrounded by six ions of opposite charge.

steps: A metal consists of positive metal ions arranged in a regular lattice and surrounded by a sea of mobile, delocalized electrons.
The electrostatic attraction between the positive ions and the mobile electrons is called a metallic bond.
The mobile electrons conduct heat and electricity through metals.
The layers of metal ions can slide over one another while remaining attracted to the electron sea, so metals are malleable and ductile.
Metals are lustrous because their free electrons reflect light.
items.finalAnswer: Metallic bonding, with positive ions held in a mobile sea of electrons, accounts for metals’ conductivity, malleability, ductility and lustre.

steps: Ionic compounds consist of positive and negative ions held together by strong electrostatic forces; covalent compounds consist of molecules in which atoms share electron pairs.
Ionic compounds are usually crystalline solids with high melting and boiling points; covalent compounds generally have lower melting and boiling points and may be gases, liquids or solids.
Ionic compounds are generally soluble in water and insoluble in organic solvents; covalent compounds are generally insoluble in water but soluble in organic solvents.
Ionic compounds conduct electricity when molten or dissolved in water, but not in the solid state because their ions cannot move freely.
Covalent compounds generally do not conduct electricity because they do not contain mobile ions or free electrons.
items.finalAnswer: Ionic compounds have ionic lattices, usually high melting points, and conduct electricity when molten or in solution; covalent compounds consist of molecules, usually have lower melting points, and generally do not conduct electricity.
